groupLabel.description: What an island is called in this town (Pillar, Team, ...).

mode.description: demo: the town runs on fake data and has the Break things panel and the story bar. live (the default when this is left out): real sources only, nothing to break. Read when the server starts.

trafficDensity.description: How many cars appear, as a multiple of the usual number: 1 is the usual look, 2 twice as many, 0.5 half. A weak PC still lowers it with the quality setting, and the town never shows more than 420 cars at once.

topology.description: Whether calls between islands go through the hub.

islands.description: Pillar codes in the order they stand round the hub: the first ringCapacity on the first ring, the rest on a staggered second ring. Pillars not listed follow in file order, and Lost & found always comes last.

ringCapacity.description: Islands on the first ring. The second ring holds one fewer, because the airport takes a place there, so a town holds at most 2 x ringCapacity - 1 pillars (23 at 12, 35 at 18). Lost & found counts as a pillar.

databaseEngines.description: The database engines this company uses, by id. A database writes engine: <id> and shows the name and type from here, so every team spells an engine the same way.

name.description: The engine as it is shown, for example Cosmos DB.

type.description: The kind of database it is. The list is fixed; every engine belongs to exactly one.

messaging.description: How this town names its message topics, and which topics are an old route.

topicTemplate.description: The name of the topic a pillar's service publishes. {pillar} and {service} are replaced.

hubTopicTemplate.description: The name of a topic of the hub. {service} is replaced by the hub's name for it.

legacyFrom.description: The owners whose topics are an old route to read. A subscription to one of them must say legacy: true.

labels.description: The words this town uses for things the app has no fixed name for.

internalVendors.description: What the town calls its own services outside the monitored platform.

wall.description: The town's defaults for wall mode. An address parameter on the page (hold, overview, light) wins over these for one screen.

holdSeconds.description: Seconds the tour stays at each stop.

overviewSeconds.description: Seconds the overview of the whole town lasts when something is wrong. 0 for no overview.

light.description: The light a wall opens in.

expectedWarnings.description: Warnings the validator should expect here: a test registry that shows a rule on purpose. They are left out of the report; if one stops appearing, that is an error.

rule.description: The rule name shown in the warning, for example standalone.

file.description: The file it is expected in, relative to the registry folder, for example pillars/sta.yaml. Leave out for any file.
